title: Exact additive Green length three for an infinite five-dimensional family
classification: Plausibly original exact-minimum theorem package; strongest current Green manuscript core
exact_claim: Let N=5q², q positive odd, gcd(q,5)=1 and q≡1 (mod 241); let F_N[i,j]=ω^(ij), A_N=diag(ω^((N+1)j²/2)), and B_N=(F_N^(-1)+A_N)^(-1). On S={0,q²,2q²,3q²,4q²}, the principal block C_q=B_N[S,S] has minimum exactly THREE terms D_L(I-W)^(-1)D_R, where W follows a Hamiltonian cycle, zero edge weights and singular endpoint masks are permitted, and every resolvent denominator is legal. The upper construction uses a genuine quadratic extension of Q(η), η=ω^(q⁴), and two reciprocal-closing-weight nontrivial branches plus a diagonal zero-weight branch. The lower bound permits all structural orders. Hence full B_N requires at least three terms, with no matching full-size upper bound established. q=1 is the accepted forced B5 case. A separate positive-Gauss-curve argument gives a non-effective finite-exception lower-bound statement.
precise_delta: A matched exact additive length, rather than a fast application formula or generic multiplicative factorization. The base obstruction exhausts all 576 ordered cycle pairs, including projective boundary charts. Principal restriction and proper specialization transfer it to an infinite arithmetic family. The new upper construction is uniform in q, with all 27 guards justified by localization and norm residues, at both quadratic roots and all primitive fifth-root embeddings. Existing cyclic-bidiagonal inverse and Green/quasiseparable representation theorems do not supply this exact minimum.
strength_and_limitations: This is an infinite-parameter family of FIXED 5-by-5 matrices, not a growing-dimensional upper construction. Three summands means two nontrivial solves and a diagonal correction. Over the base field alone the same upper length has not been established. For full B_N only the lower bound is proved. Moreover the same two-natural-cycle-plus-diagonal ansatz is impossible at every odd N≥7: its complementary cut rank is at most two, while B_N has a half-cut of rank floor(N/2). This does not exclude three terms with other structural orders. The conditional Fourier/Bluestein bridge requires a full uniform family, charged setup and compatible roots; C_q supplies none of those missing premises.
proof_status: Accepted independent reviews E01–E03 and E18. The new review seal is bcfd6469945506c291d025856353900654026159fe8ac434a189a10fa68abd5a. Actual proof/review read; no source executables replayed in this novelty pass. The lower certificate establishes geometric-fiber emptiness, not merely an empty finite-field point scan; the upper guards are uniform local-ring arguments, not extrapolations from sample q.
missing_work: Package a compact theorem-and-certificate release with a standalone checker and a human-readable explanation of the finite obstruction. State the field of definition in every length claim. A further focused additive-resolvent/secant-literature comparison remains advisable before submission. A higher-dimensional upper construction is a separate research goal and not a missing premise of the five-dimensional theorem.
plausible_manuscript_proposition: “Exact additive length in an arithmetic family of cyclic-resolvent decompositions.” Main theorem: ℓ_G(C_q)=3 for the stated infinite family; corollary: ℓ_G(B_(5q²))≥3. Supporting propositions: principal-restriction closure, closed-projective specialization, guarded reciprocal-pole synthesis.

title: Sharp endpoint-permutation quasiseparable order of dyadic Fourier matrices
classification: Plausibly original sharp extremal theorem; clean short-paper candidate
exact_claim: For N=2^m>=8 over characteristic zero, min_{rho,sigma} q(P_rho F_N P_sigma^T)=N/4+1, where q is the maximum rank over all strict upper-right and lower-left complementary cuts. Double bit reversal attains it. Its upper-right cut ranks obey r_N(k)=ceil(k/2)+r_{N/4}(floor(k/2)) for k<=N/2, with reflection symmetry. Exact total-rank minima are also established at N=8,16.
precise_delta: The all-independent-endpoint minimax value, with a second-moment/odd-cardinality lower bound matching a bit-reversal recurrence. Prior Fourier submatrix theory already contains double-digit-reversal rank-one block grids and sharp support uncertainty, so those ingredients must be credited.
strength_and_limitations: An exact all-size formula is substantially stronger than a finite screen and does not require source code. It is a rank-structure theorem, not an arithmetic lower bound: high cut rank alone does not make matrix application expensive. Characteristic-zero positivity is essential to the supplied lower-bound proof; arbitrary finite fields are outside it.
proof_status: Accepted E04; actual proof read. The official Delvaux–Van Barel TW470 preprint was inspected at Lemma 8, Theorem 10 and Sections 3–4. Accessible later primary universal-sampling/full-spark/conditioning papers were compared in the addendum. The final 2008 journal version remains unavailable in full; this is an unresolved comparison, not evidence that it lacks the theorem.
missing_work: Obtain a legitimate full copy of the final Delvaux–Van Barel 2008 article and check any changes from TW470. Make the new universal second-moment lower bound central, credit the existing double-bit-reversal hierarchy, and distinguish exact q-minimax from unproved larger-size total-rank minima.
plausible_manuscript_proposition: “The minimum quasiseparable order of a dyadic Fourier matrix under independent endpoint permutations.”

title: Three-stage quasiseparable Fourier obstruction through discrepancy
classification: Substantial new application of classical discrepancy theory
exact_claim: For F_N represented as S3 P2 S2 P1 S1 with q(S_i)<=r_i, arbitrary independent internal permutations, and at least one affine-coprime Fourier endpoint ordering, the other endpoint arbitrary, necessarily 2r1+r2+r3>=c log N-2; transposition gives r1+r2+2r3>=c log N-2. Repeated bit reversal additionally yields r1+r2+r3>=ceil(log2(N)/2), excluding rank-one stages for dyadic N>=128.
precise_delta: The bridge from cyclic-window full-rank conditions to grid discrepancy of an internal permutation. Averaging all cyclic windows gives the exact centering Wt/N; applying Schmidt then excludes every fixed-order three-stage family in this scope.
strength_and_limitations: This is an infinite-family obstruction with a conceptual connection beyond the original search. Schmidt’s lower bound and quasiseparable rank calculus are prior art. Both endpoints arbitrary and non-affine are not covered; no general arithmetic lower bound or arbitrary-depth exclusion follows.
proof_status: Accepted E05. Rank proof and cyclic averaging read. Schmidt’s original publisher record was located; its precise theorem/normalization was verified in primary paper P16 because the original PDF was inaccessible.
missing_work: Compare permutation discrepancy and low-rank factorization literature beyond keywords; decide whether to combine with the endpoint minimax theorem; extend endpoint scope or stage count if possible; do not invent an explicit c or finite cutoff from the existential discrepancy constant.
plausible_manuscript_proposition: “Permutation discrepancy as an obstruction to shallow quasiseparable Fourier factorizations.”

title: One-layer Fourier obstruction for independently ordered weighted-permutation Green sums
classification: Substantial specialized application of classical combinatorics and Fourier minors
exact_claim: Over C, F_N cannot equal a sum of r diagonally ended legal weighted-permutation resolvents, plus rank-t, row-degree-s sparse and arbitrary diagonal corrections, once N>2(m-1)(B-m)(B-1), where m=r+t+1, L=m(s+2), B=(L-1)^{2^{r-1}}+1. Independent structural cycle orders, zero weights and singular diagonal masks are allowed. Fixed t,s imply r=Omega(log log N).
precise_delta: Combines rank-one separated rectangles for each independently ordered resolvent, simultaneous monotone-subsequence extraction and a short-arc Schur-polynomial Fourier-minor argument. The arbitrary-order one-layer obstruction does not follow from the separate sparse-inverse/rank gate.
strength_and_limitations: Useful theorem for restricted linear representations; explicit r=2 threshold N>2300 and r=3 threshold N>34,545,588 are large but rigorous. Unmatched independent row/column permutations on each term are excluded. Products of layers escape the proof; the term lower bound is very weak compared with FFT arithmetic complexity.
proof_status: Accepted E14. Full all-size argument and threshold derivation read. The broad ingredients are classical; their precise combination remains a plausible new application, not confirmed historical priority.
missing_work: Search additive rank-structured decomposition and simultaneous-order/Ramsey literature; sharpen thresholds or growth if feasible; formulate general target-minor hypotheses to give a theorem beyond Fourier; explain explicitly why product grammars are not covered.
plausible_manuscript_proposition: “Additive obstructions for independently ordered cyclic resolvents and Fourier matrices.”

title: Exact recognition of common-quadratic-phase sparse Fourier sums
classification: Plausibly original exact-recognition/elimination theorem; known signal model
exact_claim: For x_j=omega^{a j^2} sum_{ell<=r} c_ell omega^{b_ell j}, over a supplied prime field/root subgroup with N>=3r, there is a sound and complete exact recognizer, with zero-vector handling. A centered normalized (r+1)-Hankel determinant has a provably nonzero constant coefficient, degree <=binom(r+2,3), and every true common phase supplies a root. Candidate recurrence recovery and full verification cost O_r(N). An accepted ring-Toeplitz extension yields a conservative uniform O(N r^4+r^{2+3 log_2 3}) bound.
precise_delta: The nonzero eliminant guaranteed for every nonzero promised input, a degree bound limiting candidate phases, parity-aware phase quotient, and charged exact membership verification. Common chirp models, rank constraints, Prony/Berlekamp–Massey and Toeplitz/Bareiss/Levinson tools are not new.
strength_and_limitations: This can support an exact symbolic/signal-recovery paper. The structured family is small; N>=3r is a sufficient bound, not established optimal identifiability. Growing r=o((log N)^{1/4}) gives a sub-N log N bound only on that structured class with a supplied field/root, not generic DFT data or stable floating point.
proof_status: Accepted E06–E07 and linked growing-rank corollary. Actual normalization, constant-term and ring-pivot reasoning read; source code not executed.
missing_work: Finish comparison with polynomial-phase Prony and finite-field sparse interpolation; make the representation equivalence classes explicit; sharpen dependence on r or show it matters practically; include rejection costs, field construction and numerical limitations.
plausible_manuscript_proposition: “A nonvanishing phase eliminant for exact common-chirp sparse Fourier recognition.”

title: Two-sided Green rectangle rank oracle and moving-interface certificates
classification: New synthesis/certification application; most structural algebra already known
exact_claim: For a legal Hamiltonian-cycle resolvent K^{-1}, rank K^{-1}[A,B]=|A|+|B|-N+rank K[B^c,A^c]. Proper support deletions leave bipartite paths, so structural rank equals maximum matching and is computable in O(N). Independent endpoint permutations/masks can be tracked. Product certificates use arbitrary intermediate sets and rank(AB)[R,C]<=rank B[S,C]+rank A[R,S^c]. The two-stage cut objective is submodular and polynomially optimizable by known oracle methods.
precise_delta: A usable exact support-aware oracle and moving-cut certificate specialized to the branch grammar, including a concrete Fourier spectral-error witness. Nullity duality, graph rank closure and submodular minimization are prior results.
strength_and_limitations: Potential framework section or software-assisted certification paper if demonstrated on a broad class. A single oracle/certificate can be linear time, but optimization is not thereby linear. Exact ranks with singular endpoint masks require deleting their supported coordinates rather than silently retaining equality.
proof_status: Accepted E08. Exact support/forest proof and optimization scope read.
missing_work: State the distinct costs of oracle, optimization and matrix execution; compare directly with graph-induced rank structures; add a general separation or an algorithmic improvement rather than recasting known inequalities.
plausible_manuscript_proposition: “Support-aware cut certificates for products of cyclic resolvents.”

title: Marked-tree constant-input jets and exact forbidden-run frontiers
classification: Useful specialized structural lemma and evaluator analysis
exact_claim: For the doubling-tree A0 and stationary root projector E, (I-z A0)^{-1}=K(z)+E/(1-z), with K=sum_{t<n}z^t(A0^t-E). Constant-input full polynomial jets have total coefficient capacity <=2N-2 and can be formed in O(N). For a retained suffix 0^b, the explicit frontier evaluator has exact F_L=2^{n-d_L} A_b(d_L), d_L=min(n,b+L), and total cost Theta(N min(n+1,2^b)), where A_b counts binary words avoiding 0^b.
precise_delta: The precise cancellation/valuation ledger for this marked tree and the exact b-dependent count for this evaluator. Finite nilpotent resolvents, tree dynamic programming, Schur complements and forbidden-word recurrences are established mathematics.
strength_and_limitations: The linear constant-input jet is real positive progress. It does not imply a linear solver for polynomial-valued unknowns or an inexpensive inverse of the border. The frontier lower bound applies to the specified explicit representation, not every algorithm.
proof_status: Accepted E09 and its linked root-pole proof. One next-pivot constant-input closure was accepted; arbitrary repeated polynomial-input closure is not.
missing_work: Extract a general theorem for a nontrivial class of functional graphs or valuation-weighted trees; compare total path-length/output-sensitive algorithms; resolve polynomial-input closure for a stronger algorithmic contribution.
plausible_manuscript_proposition: “Output-sensitive polynomial jets on marked functional trees and their frontier growth.”

title: Universal reciprocal factorization of adjacent Hankel-pencil resultants
classification: Possibly original explicit formula/application; modest standalone significance after broader-pencil comparison
exact_claim: Let m=s+1, P_e(a,w)=det[T_{e+i+j}(1-a w^{e+i+j})] for e=0,1 and 0<=i,j<m, with formal independent T_0,...,T_{2s+1}. With fixed-degree-m Sylvester resultant R_s=Res_a(P_0,P_1), D=m^2(2m-1), v=s(s+1)(4s+5)/6 and b=s(s+1)(2s+1)/6: w^D R_s(1/w)=(-1)^{m^2}R_s(w), R_s=w^v(w-1)^{m^2}U_s, w^{2b}U_s(1/w)=U_s(w), and U_s=w^b V_s(w+w^{-1}) with deg V_s<=b. The valuation v is generically exact; all identities survive singular and zero-resultant specializations.
precise_delta: The explicit factors, closed-form generic zero valuation and compressed degree are the identifiable formula-level delta. The same complete package holds for arbitrary coefficient matrices A,B in det(A−aDAD), det(B−awDBD), so adjacency and Hankel structure are unnecessary for these identities. Standard resultant transformation laws, mixed-minor expansions and unequal-slope Newton valuation rules provide the mechanism. No inspected primary source literally states this exact formula; that is not a global novelty conclusion.
strength_and_limitations: Correct and useful all-s algebra, but the broad-pencil derivation is short once standard machinery is recognized. Compression reduces a degree with cubic growth in s by a constant factor; it does not establish an asymptotic elimination breakthrough. A standalone substantial manuscript would need a stronger recovery theorem, broader classification or demonstrated algorithmic advance. Its supplied fixed-s application is conditional on nonzero probes, a nonzero resultant, a linear gcd and spectral invertibility. It is not an all-input generic FFT.
proof_status: The Hankel specialization is accepted E17. The arbitrary-matrix generalization and its symbolic proof are assessment-level work in ADDENDUM_20261010_0149.md, corroborated by six fresh small fixed-degree Sylvester controls, and are NOT separately independently reviewed. No submitted research program was executed.
missing_work: Keep the precise universal identity as a lemma or compact note; do not frame it as a new elimination method or intrinsically Hankel phenomenon. Independently check the broader-pencil derivation before incorporating it into a manuscript. Establish a stronger application or structural classification before assigning standalone publication priority.
plausible_manuscript_proposition: “Universal factors in diagonally scaled matrix-pencil resultants.” A short theorem/technical appendix with the explicit exponents; the sparse-rational recovery application must carry its guards and cost model.

title: Exact N16 coefficient existence certificate
classification: New finite construction plus reproducible certification engineering
exact_claim: An exact F16 exists in the fixed model H2 H1 B H0 with eight fixed Hamiltonian routes/poles per layer, 24 branch occurrences and 384 complex endpoint parameters. In a 256-dimensional affine chart, a rational contraction certificate isolates a unique root within radius 10^{-9}; it proves nonzero endpoint margins and the full matrix equality.
precise_delta: An exact reproducible witness for this particular constrained architecture, replacing a floating residual. Rational nonlinear-root certification itself is established.
strength_and_limitations: Worth preserving as a benchmark/counterexample and appendix. The parameters exceed N^2, and the result has no uniform coefficient generator, growing-size theorem, synthesis complexity bound or cost advantage. “Positive coefficient certificate” means affirmative existence, not positive real coefficients.
proof_status: Accepted E10 with exact rational contraction bounds, not just supplied optimizer output. This novelty pass read the audit, without rerunning it.
missing_work: Find a compact algebraic pattern, parameter compression, minimality or an infinite lift; otherwise do not build the main publication claim around one overparameterized N16 fit.
plausible_manuscript_proposition: “A certified finite Fourier factorization in a fixed cyclic-resolvent architecture,” as an example within a broader theorem paper.

title: Projective graph constraint solver
classification: Known core over C; possible new field-general implementation and Green application
exact_claim: Solve selected constraints u_k^T L_e u_i=0 on P1: invertible edges transport projective directions; cycle closures restrict a component to all P1, at most two points, or empty; rank-one edges become equality-literal disjunctions treated by 2-SAT and domain consistency. The accepted treatment includes infinity, repeated roots, characteristic two and algebraic-closure rejection by polynomial gcd.
precise_delta: The finite-field/arbitrary-characteristic details and extraction from Green off-support equations may be useful additions. Over C the same bilinear product-vector constraints, transfer matrices, cycle eigenvectors and singular-edge logic already occur in quantum 2-SAT algorithms.
strength_and_limitations: Do not claim a new general projective constraint-solving paradigm. The result solves a selected necessary row subsystem only; it does not finish column compatibility or scales, so success is not a Green factorization. This is the clearest novelty downgrade of the pass.
proof_status: Accepted E11 as a mathematical/algorithmic result. Its historical novelty was not certified by the local review. Primary quantum-2SAT texts were compared directly.
missing_work: Write an explicit reduction and theorem-by-theorem comparison with quantum 2-SAT; identify a genuinely absent characteristic/domain/complexity guarantee; position as a specialization unless that delta is substantial.
plausible_manuscript_proposition: “Projective constraint propagation over general fields for cyclic-resolvent feasibility,” with quantum-2SAT attribution.

title: Uniform sparse-inverse and low-rank perturbation gates
classification: Elementary corollaries of known uncertainty and rank identities
exact_claim: If F=product_i H_i, H_i=G_i+R_i with invertible H_i,G_i, rank R_i<=r_i and column sparsity of G_i^{-1} at most s_i, then with r=sum r_i and s=product s_i, s(r+1)^2>=N. For a prime complex Fourier transform, (s+1)(r+1)>=p+1. Stage-count/work consequences require the stated fully materialized per-stage executor.
precise_delta: A clean scope ledger and reusable test for a proposed circuit grammar. Inverse-difference telescoping, a sparse kernel vector and classical support uncertainty give the inequalities directly; no new general uncertainty theorem is supplied.
strength_and_limitations: Useful lemmas and guards, unlikely standalone publication substance. Dense structured high-rank corrections and other executors remain outside the cost inference; prime complex additive uncertainty must not be copied to arbitrary finite fields.
proof_status: Accepted E12, including field limitations. The proof was read.
missing_work: Attribute the standard ingredients and retain as a proposition supporting a genuinely new representation theorem; avoid upgrading a restricted rank/cost gate into a general FFT lower bound.
plausible_manuscript_proposition: “Uncertainty-based necessary conditions for sparse-inverse perturbation circuits,” as a supporting proposition.

title: Aggregate-fiber sparse recognizer
classification: Known sparse-recovery tools with a useful fully charged promise
exact_claim: With N=QM and total fiber modes <=K0, exact recognition and full output can be charged O(N+M K0+Q K0+K0^2). If K0=O(Q) and Q^2<=N, this becomes O(N), with rejected-input processing explicitly bounded.
precise_delta: An aggregate rather than per-fiber promise and careful heavy/light accounting. Recurrence recovery, root enumeration, Vandermonde recovery and exact verification are standard.
strength_and_limitations: Potential application or corollary; no generic-input transform improvement. Novelty is more likely in the precise recognition guarantee and accounting than the core algorithm.
proof_status: Accepted E13; reviewed theorem and scope.
missing_work: Compare closely with block sparse interpolation and sparse Fourier recovery; show a meaningful regime or new worst-case dependence beyond reassembling standard primitives.
plausible_manuscript_proposition: “Exact aggregate-sparsity recognition for Fourier fibers,” as a corollary or applications section.

title: Fixed-direction completion and fixed-pencil exclusion certificates
classification: Application/engineering evidence rather than a main new theorem
exact_claim: For fixed projective row/column directions, full off-support vanishing plus supported affine scale equations and nonzero scale/cycle guards characterize invertible branch completion. Separately, several fixed-mask, one-parameter Green pencils are excluded by exact projective cross-ratios and modular nonzero resultants at specified finite sizes.
precise_delta: The exact specialization to these search grammars and independently checkable certificates. Sparse affine graph solving, projective invariants, resultants and saturation/guard discipline are established techniques.
strength_and_limitations: Valuable reproducibility and search-space reduction. Fixed directions do not solve the full nonlinear problem, and fixed-pencil exclusions do not exclude the encompassing family. These belong with the successful construction/lower-bound paper rather than being promoted individually.
proof_status: Accepted E15–E16 within their exact scopes. No broad representation theorem inferred.
missing_work: Unify into a compact certificate format, preserve all guards, document verification versus discovery cost, and demonstrate a reusable mathematical consequence.
plausible_manuscript_proposition: “Exact feasibility certificates for fixed cyclic-resolvent directions,” as a methods appendix.
